---
title: "A5 exercises — Signals, muscle and reproduction"
---

Use the [tutorial](index.qmd). Values and response descriptions are invented
teaching examples. These tasks require no recordings, stimulation or human/
animal intervention. Allow 60–90 minutes. Leave with a linked response pathway,
one work/power calculation and a reproductive feedback explanation.

## 1. Repair a membrane explanation

A student writes: “The sodium pump opens when the neuron fires, pushes sodium
into the cell, and makes a bigger spike when the stimulus is stronger.”
Identify at least three errors. Replace the account with ion gradients,
selective channels, a representative action-potential sequence and one way
stronger stimulation can be encoded.

What must be known, besides channel identity, to determine the direction
of net ion movement?

## 2. Trace a reflex and a synapse

Draw stimulus → sensory receptor/afferent → integration → motor neuron →
effector. Expand one chemical synapse to include presynaptic electrical change,
calcium entry, transmitter release, receptor binding and postsynaptic effect.

Explain why a neurotransmitter name alone does not prove whether the receiving
cell will be excited or inhibited. Which part of a simple withdrawal pathway
need not wait for conscious decision?

## 3. Link excitation to contraction

Create an ordered account from a motor-neuron action potential to skeletal
muscle force and then relaxation. Include the neuromuscular junction,
muscle electrical activity, calcium release, regulatory proteins, actin–myosin
cycling, ATP and calcium recovery. Explain why ATP is needed even when
the muscle eventually relaxes.

An invented skeletal-muscle section contains long striated fibres with many
nuclei. Which features support that interpretation? Contrast it with smooth
and cardiac muscle, without treating a textual description as real-slide
recognition.

## 4. Keep work, power and ATP use separate

A hypothetical muscle lifts a load with a constant force of 20 N through
0.10 m in 0.50 s. Force and displacement are aligned. Calculate external
mechanical work and mean external mechanical power.

It then holds the load at the same height for 5 s. Calculate external work
over that stationary interval using $W=Fd$. Does your answer establish that
ATP consumption is zero? Explain. What would be needed to estimate metabolic
efficiency rather than external work alone?

## 5. Compare hormones and responses

Two target tissues are exposed to the same circulating hormone concentration,
but one changes its activity and the other does not. Give three possible
mechanistic explanations that do not require a measurement error. Distinguish
a surface-receptor pathway from an intracellular-receptor pathway, and explain
why neither the words “neural” nor “endocrine” alone fixes response duration.

## 6. Bring reproduction and the whole animal together

Draw a mammalian hypothalamus → pituitary → gonad axis. Label GnRH,
gonadotropins and a gonadal feedback signal. Explain the usual stabilising
role of negative feedback and the different role of positive feedback around
the pre-ovulatory LH surge under appropriate conditions.

Then write 150–200 words tracing a terrestrial animal's escape response
through sensation, muscle recruitment, ATP demand, oxygen transport and heat/
water costs. Identify one immediate response and one sustained adjustment.
Finish by explaining why resource availability can also influence reproductive
investment. Check your concepts with the [quiz](quiz.qmd).
